title: 刘欣璇（Elena Liu）
text:
欢迎来到我的个人主页！
我目前是英国萨里大学经济学博士研究生。我的研究兴趣包括宏观金融、金融稳定与最优政策。


我的中文名字是欣璇，英文名是 Elena。English Version / 英文版


欢迎联系！


非常欢迎与我交流想法、学术合作及工作机会。当然，如果你愿意赞助一份英国超市的 Meal Deal，帮助我度过博士阶段的最后冲刺，我也会非常感激！ :)


邮箱： xinxuan.liu@surrey.ac.uk · xinxuan.elena.liu@gmail.com







我的研究关注金融市场如何促进风险分担、政府债券如何获得其避险资产价值，以及金融衍生品和监管政策如何影响这些机制。我主要运用静态、离散时间和连续时间一般均衡模型，将资产定价、宏观审慎政策与货币政策相结合，研究相关经济学问题。


工作论文 · 与 Mário Páscoa 合作


摘要


本文研究当标的证券同时作为融资市场中的抵押品时，禁止裸信用违约互换（CDS）所产生的影响。我们构建了一个连接证券市场、回购融资市场与 CDS 市场的一般均衡模型。在这一框架中，CDS 的持券覆盖要求不仅改变投资者的风险对冲机会，也会影响稀缺抵押品在不同金融市场之间的配置。监管政策的影响在很大程度上取决于标的证券对宏观经济状态的风险暴露。当证券具有避险资产属性时，覆盖要求可能使抵押品退出回购市场，并压低证券价格。相反，当证券具有顺周期属性时，同样的监管措施可能支撑资产价格并降低 CDS 溢价。本文揭示了旨在限制投机活动的监管措施如何通过抵押品稀缺及金融市场之间的相互联系产生非预期后果。





工作论文


摘要


本文研究私人风险分担、政府债券的安全资产价值与宏观审慎政策之间的相互作用。我构建了一个连续时间一般均衡模型，其中异质性家庭面临特质风险，并通过向金融中介购买看跌期权来对冲下行风险。私人保险在改善风险分担的同时，也会改变家庭对政府债券的需求。政府债券的价值部分来源于其支持跨期财富转移和动态交易的功能。金融中介受到杠杆约束，因此其风险承担能力、私人对冲机会与均衡资产价格之间存在内在联系。通过比较分散化市场均衡与约束有效配置，本文考察不完全风险分担的福利后果，以及宏观审慎监管可能发挥的作用。研究强调，针对金融中介的监管政策不仅影响私人保险市场，也可能改变安全资产的均衡估值。





进行中的研究


摘要


本项目构建一个包含银行存款与数字货币的理论框架，研究中国人口老龄化如何与金融中介活动、货币政策传导及社会福利相互作用。

title: Xinxuan (Elena) Liu
text:
Welcome to my webpage!
I am a PhD researcher in Economics at the University of Surrey. My research interests include macro-finance, financial stability, and optimal policy.


*My Chinese name is Xinxuan (欣璇), and I also go by Elena. A Chinese version of my webpage is available here.（中文版请点击这里。）


Get in touch!


I am always happy to hear about ideas, collaborations, and job opportunities - or if you simply feel like sponsoring a meal deal to help me survive the final stretch of my PhD :)


Email: xinxuan.liu@surrey.ac.uk · xinxuan.elena.liu@gmail.com







My research explores how financial markets facilitate risk sharing, how government bonds derive their safe-haven value, and how financial derivatives and regulation shape these mechanisms. I address these questions using general equilibrium models in static, discrete-time, and continuous-time settings, integrating asset pricing, and macroprudential and monetary policy.


Working paper · with Mário Páscoa


Abstract


This paper examines the effects of banning naked sovereign credit default swaps (CDS) when the underlying securities serve as collateral in funding markets. We develop a general equilibrium model linking securities, repo financing, and CDS markets, in which CDS covering requirements alter both investors’ hedging opportunities and the allocation of scarce collateral. The effects of regulation depend critically on the underlying securities’ exposure to aggregate state. When securities behave as safe-haven assets, covering requirements can withdraw collateral from repo markets and depress security prices. In contrast, when securities are procyclical, the same regulation can support asset prices and reduce CDS premia. Our analysis highlights how restrictions intended to reduce speculative activity can generate unintended consequences through collateral scarcity and interconnected financial markets.





Working paper


Abstract


This paper studies the interaction between private risk sharing, the safe-asset value of government bonds, and macroprudential policy. I develop a continuous-time general equilibrium model in which heterogeneous households face idiosyncratic risk and purchase put options from financial intermediaries to hedge downside exposure. While private insurance improves risk sharing, it also changes households’ demand for government bonds, whose value partly reflects their role in facilitating intertemporal wealth transfers and dynamic trading. Financial intermediaries are subject to leverage constraints, creating a link between their risk-bearing capacity, private hedging opportunities, and equilibrium asset prices. I compare the decentralized equilibrium with a constrained-efficient benchmark to investigate the welfare consequences of incomplete risk sharing and the potential role of macroprudential regulation. The analysis highlights how policies governing financial intermediaries can affect both private insurance markets and the valuation of safe assets.





Work in progress


Abstract


This project develops a theoretical framework incorporating bank deposits and digital currency to investigate how population ageing in China interacts with financial intermediation, monetary policy transmission, and welfare.
